Warbler drive-test report (app version 1.1)

Signal Sense · instrument validation · export 20261117 · sessions Oct 16 – Nov 17, 8 sessions

Objective. Check that the Warbler app captures the data planned for QoE drive tests, and whether the data are correct or show anomalies. 2 phones, one carrier (US Mobile on AT&T, MCC 310 / MNC 410), US vantage. This validates the instrument; it says nothing about network performance in the study area.

Note. NDT7 accounts for 96–100% of the data in every session. G.1051 uses about 2 MB per test and WebRTC about 10 MB per call, both small. (Session 1's G.1051 bytes are missing because that older build didn't record them.)

What this still misses: the Plane 2/3 bursts don't record how many bytes they download, and the app's own uploads to the ava server aren't counted anywhere.

3. Completeness and joins

Radio and joins are field-ready. Location, RSRP, RSRQ, SINR, cell ID, PCI, MCC/MNC and connection type are at most 0.0% null across all 27,414 samples. 470 of 470 burst probes join to a radio sample within 1 s. NDT7 and G.1051 records carry the drive-session ID.

Still missing from the spec: transport on each burst probe, DNS resolver identity and private-DNS flag, ASN/geolocation of target IPs, a cold-connection flag, cache status and CDN PoP, NDT7 loss and latency fields, and data use of bursts and app uploads (details in Section 9).

The app records LTE only. All 6 5G fields (override_network_type, nr_rsrp, nr_sinr, gnb_id, nr_cell_id, nci) are empty on every row, so any time the phone is on 5G NSA, the data still reports LTE.

4. Cadence conformance

A Plane 2/3 burst connects to all 10 targets back-to-back within about 11 seconds, recording DNS, TCP connect, TLS and TTFB times for each. Because every target is measured on the same cell under the same radio conditions, differences between targets reflect the path to the content, not the signal.

Radio: 1 Hz with no gaps (largest gap 1.09 s).
Bursts: every 10.6 min (median). A burst takes 10.9 s (median; 90th percentile 13.9 s; 1 outlier at 113 s). During a burst the phone moved a median of 7 m, 90th percentile 89 m, maximum 219 m. 1 bursts spanned a cell change.

Observations.
  • Implausible minimum RTT on cellular. Median 7.7 ms (32 of 47 tests to New York servers), lower than Wi-Fi (40.6 ms). G.1051, measured from the phone, shows ~45 ms. Likely the server is timing a connection to a carrier middlebox, not to the phone.
  • Very high cellular throughput reported as LTE (median 324 Mbps), consistent with 5G NSA, which the app cannot detect (Section 3).
  • Empty on every test: retransmission / loss, latency under load, idle latency, jitter, udp rtt / loss, aim scores, stream count. The reference baseline in the spec (throughput, RTT, loss) is incomplete without retransmission/loss.

7. TTFB results and observations

Each probe reports DNS lookup, TCP connect (τ_TCP), TLS handshake and TTFB times. The spec defines TTFB as the total time to the first byte: TTFB = DNS + TCP + TLS + first-byte wait, so TTFB should never be smaller than DNS + TCP + TLS. 369 successful probes are checked below.

Medians by target (ms)

Consistency checks

CheckProbesShare
TTFB < DNS + TCP + TLS167 of 36945%
TTFB < TLS71 of 36919%
TTFB < DNS51 of 36914%
TTFB < TCP connect (one RTT)3 of 3691%
Anomaly: TTFB does not match the spec definition. In 45% of probes TTFB is smaller than DNS + TCP + TLS, and in 14% smaller than DNS alone. The pattern is target-specific (cloudflare 100%, daraz 98%, youtube 76%, facebook 62%; but tiktok 7%, bkash 7%, pathao 6%, whatsapp 2%), while TTFB is below one RTT in only 3 probes. This is consistent with the app measuring only the request-to-first-byte phase (the spec's τ_First-Byte), not cumulative TTFB. To be confirmed with the developer.
Other observations.
  • Daraz is abnormally slow to set up: median DNS 977 ms and TLS 1183 ms, against ~62 ms and ~111 ms for other targets. 40 of 49 DNS lookups above 500 ms are Daraz.
  • TLS takes about 3 RTTs (median 118 ms vs τ_TCP 35 ms), more than a TLS 1.3 handshake needs; the TLS timer may include certificate verification on the phone.

8. WebRTC and G.1051 results and observations

G.1051 sends a 15-second call-shaped UDP stream (pattern video_chat_hd) to a reflector and measures RTT, delay variation and loss under load. Observations.
  • Delay variation is higher on Wi-Fi: G.1051 PDV 33.7 ms on Wi-Fi vs 11.6 ms on cellular, with similar RTT; worst G.1051 loss 46.3% on Wi-Fi vs 6.4% on cellular.
  • G.1051 reflector is ava.cs.vt.edu, so G.1051 RTT measures the path to that host. In Dhaka this would be an international path.
  • WebRTC records do not identify the server or peer the call connected to, so its path (on-net, in-country, international) cannot be determined. network_type is always default, so transport is inferred from radio samples.
  • G.1051 also reports pdq, il, dpdv, ddq and intact; however, their definitions are not yet clear and need to be discussed.

9. Summary: missing data, anomalies and updates required

Issue tracker: Warbler app issues (Google Sheet)

#TypeItemEvidence in this exportUpdate requiredSeverity
1Missing5G fieldsAll 6 5G fields are empty on every sample, so the app reports LTE only, even on 5G NSAPopulate the existing empty fields in drive_samples: nci, gnb_id, nr_cell_id, override_network_type, nr_rsrp, nr_sinrBlocker
2MissingTransport per probePlane 2/3 bursts carry no transport field; transport is inferred by joining each probe to the nearest radio sampleStamp each Plane 2/3 burst probe with the network it used: transport (cellular / wifi / vpn) and display_network_type (LTE / 5G NSA / 5G SA) at the moment it ranLow
3MissingDNS resolver identity and private-DNS flagNot recorded. τ_DNS can't be attributed to the operator's resolver vs a third-party one (e.g. Google), and the choice of target server can't be explainedAdd to each Plane 2/3 burst probe: resolver_ip, private_dns_active (true / false), private_dns_server (e.g. dns.google, if set)Blocker
4MissingASN / geolocation of target IPtarget_ip is recorded, but no ASN or location is attached, so on-net / off-net / international can't be determined from the dataAt ingest, look up each target_ip and add: target_asn, target_as_name, target_country, target_city, geo_source, geo_db_date. From these, tag each probe as on-net (ASN = operator), off-net in-country or international in path_tierNormal
5MissingCold connection (connection reuse)Not recorded. No 0 ms DNS lookups suggests DNS isn't cached, but nothing confirms that TCP and TLS connections were fresh. A reused connection skips DNS, TCP and TLS, which would make τ_TCP invalidEvery Plane 2/3 burst probe must open a new connection (fresh DNS lookup, new TCP and TLS handshake). Record connection_reused (true / false) on each probe to prove it; any probe with true is flagged and excluded from the analysisBlocker
6MissingCache status and CDN PoPNot recorded, so it's unknown whether content was served from an edge cache or fetched from the origin, even when the target server is in-countryRecord from each Plane 2/3 burst probe's response headers: cache_status (e.g. HIT / MISS, from cf-cache-status or x-cache), cdn_pop (serving location, e.g. from cf-ray), server_header, via_headerNormal
7MissingNDT7 loss and latency fieldsThese fields exist in throughput_records but are empty on all 47 tests: packet_loss, loaded_latency_ms, unloaded_latency_ms, jitter_ms, udp_rtt_ms, udp_loss_count, aim_streaming, aim_gaming, aim_video, streams. Only minimum RTT is recorded, and on cellular it looks implausibly lowPopulate from the TCP statistics the M-Lab server reports during each test: packet_loss (retransmission ratio), rtt_ms (median RTT during the test, not just the minimum), jitter_ms (RTT variation), loaded_latency_ms, unloaded_latency_ms. Populate the remaining fields where NDT7 provides themBlocker
8MissingData use of bursts and app uploadsOnly NDT7, G.1051 and WebRTC record bytes. Plane 2/3 bursts record none, and the app's uploads to the ava server aren't counted, so total data use per session is underestimatedAdd response_bytes to each Plane 2/3 burst probe; add app_rx_bytes and app_tx_bytes to each session (from Android's per-app counters at session start and end)Low
9MissingWebRTC server/peer and transportWebRTC records don't identify the server or peer the call connected to, so the call's path (on-net, in-country, international) can't be determined. network_type is always default, so transport is inferred from radio samplesRecord from each call's selected ICE candidate pair: remote_ip (the other end of the call), candidate_type (host / srflx / relay), protocol (udp / tcp), and transport (cellular / wifi)Normal
10AnomalyTTFB definitionPer the spec, TTFB = DNS + TCP + TLS + first-byte wait, so it can never be smaller than DNS + TCP + TLS. Yet TTFB is smaller than DNS + TCP + TLS in 45% of probes and smaller than DNS alone in 14%. TTFB is below one RTT in only 1%, which suggests the app measures only the request-to-first-byte waitConfirm what ttfb_ms measures and document each timer's start and end point. Record both on each Plane 2/3 burst probe: ttfb_total_ms (from the start of the DNS lookup to the first response byte) and first_byte_ms (from request sent to first response byte)Blocker
